required_evidence: Characterize exactly which irrational alpha make N_alpha surjective on smooth complex zero-mean functions, and justify uniqueness and both directions of the characterization. A finite polynomial small-divisor lower bound, the equivalent rational-approximation condition, or an equivalent correctly proved formulation is sufficient.

Determine all nonnegative Sobolev losses s under the stated quantifiers, including an exact criterion at the endpoint. Establish both sufficiency and necessity; a one-sided sufficient bound is incomplete.
For alpha=sqrt(2)-1, prove that the smallest Sobolev loss is 1 and is attained, with a valid obstruction for every smaller nonnegative loss.

Prove the requested C^(m+4)-to-C^m estimate for every nonnegative integer m, with a finite constant independent of the smooth forcing. A stronger valid estimate that implies this bound is also accepted.
critical_errors: Treat irrationality and nonzero Fourier divisors as sufficient for a smooth inverse on every smooth forcing without controlling the growth of their reciprocals.

Replace the claim that every smooth forcing has a smooth solution by a separate bad frequency for each proposed norm bound without bridging the quantifiers; a valid closed-graph argument is an accepted bridge.
Infer an endpoint estimate from estimates for every strictly larger loss, or assert the endpoint is always attained without its uniform arithmetic bound.
Silently remove the zero-mean condition or assert uniqueness without controlling the constant Fourier coefficient.
Use only a C^(m+5)-to-C^m estimate and report the C^(m+4)-to-C^m target completed, reversing the inequality between the input norms.
Conflate the optimal one-derivative Sobolev loss with an unsupported one-derivative C^m estimate, or assert four is the optimal C^m loss without proof.
Claim that a weaker formal estimate, or this extracted task, refutes the original Navier-Stokes theorem.
completion_policy: Complete the general smooth-solvability and loss classification, plus the fixed-direction minimum and C^m estimate. Accept short correct arguments and verified applicable theorems; do not require the author's explicit bad forcing, Pell sequence, irrationality exponent, exact best constant, Fourier summability proof route, or any optional extension. An exact arithmetic endpoint criterion is sufficient; an additional example with an unattained endpoint is not required.
open_task_policy: Accept independently verified alternative proofs, equivalent arithmetic criteria, and unexpected valid results. Explicit conditional results are legitimate contributions, but do not complete the unconditioned classification unless all cases are covered. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
